title: Unpaid household production is a large part of the economy even when GDP leaves it out
source_unit: BEA household production statistics integrated with market activities and supply-and-use framework

observations.period: 2024; household production integrated with market activities

denominator.unit: U.S. consumption and total-output accounting framework

observations.method: BEA household-production statistics integrated with market activities; the measures estimate the contribution of unpaid household activities in an expanded accounting framework.
observations.uncertainty: The source reports approximate national shares; account definitions, valuation choices, source data, and integration with supply-and-use tables shape the estimates.
observations.subgroup: U.S. national economy; household production across seven activity types in the expanded update.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large measured share does not establish that the work was fairly distributed, freely chosen, high quality, or a burden rather than a valued activity.

observations.method: BEA summary of the updated household-production statistics and long-run share movement.
observations.uncertainty: The summary does not identify the contribution of prices, household composition, market substitution, activity definitions, or changes in unpaid-work volume to the declining shares.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower household-production share can mean more market production or different accounting composition, not necessarily less unpaid work or more household freedom.

denominator.unit: household activity types with expanded value-added detail

new_measure_layers.value: spending and gross output in addition to value added

observations.method: BEA description of the June 2026 update, including childcare and shopping and integration within the supply-and-use framework.
observations.uncertainty: This is an accounting-coverage improvement, not evidence that household outcomes or measurement of individual burden improved.
observations.counterinterpretation: More detailed accounting can make an activity visible without changing who controls, performs, or benefits from it.

boundary: This record makes unpaid household production visible in national accounting and records a long-run share direction. It does not measure who performs the work, choice, exhaustion, quality, substitution, distribution, wellbeing, care adequacy, or household security, and it is not a same-household outcome estimate.
